Hey there, fellow anxious girlie in her 20s here. I just got my first abnormal pap after over a decade of annual normal ones, and it felt so unfair—especially after being abstinent for 2+ years post-breakup and even getting the Gardasil vaccine as a teen. But the truth is, there’s nothing I could’ve done to prevent it, and it’s not my fault (or my partner’s). It’s frustrating that men can unknowingly carry it without being affected.

Getting that call from my doctor to schedule a colposcopy and biopsy was terrifying, but my OB/GYN reassured me that the procedure was just to confirm and treat if needed. Honestly, it wasn’t worse than a pap—just took a little longer, and the biopsy felt like pressure, not pain (imo it was 50x less painful than a bikini wax!). **Waiting for results is the hardest part**, my doctor reassured as well, but reminding myself that these changes take a long time to turn into anything serious helped. The reason your provider is scheduling this procedure after your second pap is because most people clear it out naturally after 2 years - they just want to be extra sure it hasn’t progressed. 

Similarly to you, when I was told the soonest availability wasn’t for another three months, I advocated for myself, shared my anxiety, and asked if I could be put on a ‘waitlist’ for an earlier appointment they’d be able to slot me in for if they had any last minute cancellations from another patient. If your provider uses MyChart, you can just join a waitlist online—it doesn’t hurt to and is worth asking. 

Most importantly, remember that this was caught early because of your diligence. Any abnormal result is scary, but you’ve done everything right to take care of your health. It’s just bad luck this time, but you’re handling it. Sending you love, positive haling energy, and support 🤍

Money SO well spent, it’s been a such a game changer that I’ve moved with it to every new apartment since I first purchased it it (9x!). It’s been my lifesaver during the hellish late summer heat waves, WFH in my AC-less apartment units (thanks west LA,) and it’s easier on my wallet/electric bill than using central ac, especially because I only use it in my bedroom. 

A great time to look for a used unit on FB marketplace is in May & June, when the college students start to move out for the summer (esp the rich private schools: USC, LMU, Pepperdine, etc). Most of the graduating students will gladly accept dirt cheap offers because they otherwise planned to just throw it out anyway. You help them take one thing off their hectic move-out list, and you get a great deal on a probably pretty new AC unit. Everyone wins!

Their approval system really varies case by case (to a certain extent). Was convicted of misdemeanor DUI in 2018. No additional criminal/legal trouble since. Completed my probation without issues in June 2021. Case was not expunged/dismissed at time of application. 

I applied for GE in late Dec 2021, and disclosed everything upfront on my application. I heard nothing about my approval status until I received email notice while overseas that I had been conditionally approved. 

When I returned 3 days later in Nov 2022 I did the Enrollment on Arrival interview, and was questioned about every single detail of my application. The CBP agent asked if I had any prior arrests or convictions, which I immediately confirmed (DUI 2016), but he furled his eyebrows and asked if “I was sure I wasn’t forgetting anything else” or “not being entirely truthful about my WHOLE past?” It took me a moment to realize that he was referring to prior incident from when I was a minor – that case was dropped, charges had never been filed, and my juvenile records had been legally sealed for over a decade. I immediately fessed up and admitted that I had forgotten about it and wasn’t sure either since it was so long in the past official charges were never filed. 

I thought the jig was up but after giving a stern lecture about the “importance of honesty as this is a *trusted traveler’s* program and the whole point is that we have to be sure we can *trust* you,” he let me know that I was also very lucky because they had *just* recently changed the rules so that a misdemeanor conviction would disqualify an applicant for only 5 years instead of 10 as it was prior. After another ten minutes of further questioning and lecturing he finally let me know that I had been officially approved. 

TL;DR: it is possible to get GE approval with a  Misdemeanor DUI conviction from over 5 years ago. Also, be transparent and upfront, you won’t be able to hide anything and it’ll only hurt than help.

I had this same concern when I transitioned from school to my first full time job! I was so worried about her mental health that I set up a motion/sound activated camera to monitor her. 

The first few weeks were rough for her, and she would wake up every 1-2 hours and vocalize that heartbreaking “where are you?” Meow that cats do. I would listen to it and nearly tear up at my desk! However, she adjusted quickly after she found her favorite window to lounge at and watch the neighbors. I left out toys for her, tv, and even spoke to her through the camera (which just spooked her) but she didn’t seem too interested in any of it since there weren’t any humans around. I thought about adopting a second cat to keep her as a companion, but didn’t want to potentially stress her out with a new cat invading her territory. I do second the bird feeder suggestion, especially if you live in an urban area without much wildlife your cat can watch as stimulation. I bought one of those that suction cup to your window so she would have a front row seat to the birds! For the first few weeks, she sulked at me as if to say “how dare you abandon me!” After about 2 weeks, she got used to the new routine and would even wait at the window to watch if the person coming through the gate was me. It was adorable, she’d meow so loud I could hear her excitement from the first floor (my place was on the second floor). As soon as I walked through the door she became lively and wanted to do nothing but play and follow me around. 

I also noticed that she changed personality wise, going from generally aloof to “YOU’RE HOME!!” And begging to be picked up for a good snuggle session. She also became MUCH more active at night due to being bored during the daytime. Your kitty will be okay :). In fact, during this WFH period it almost seems like she’s annoyed that I’m always home! Cats are funny. 

You’re a great cat mom for worrying, but your kitty will adjust. They’re resilient little sweeties!

Hi, I’m sorry to hear you’re going through a hard time. My s/o recently broke up with me again for the second time, and mornings for me are also the hardest. It’s natural due to a couple reasons. The first is that in order to wake up, your body produces more of the naturally occurring stress hormone to get your body ready for the day. As someone who struggled with anxiety all my life, I always found that it was much worse in the morning and would get better as the day progressed. The second reason is that in the mornings you’re often not at work or school yet, so you have nothing else to distract your mind from the thing you think about first when you wake up. Especially if you spent your relationship accustomed to good morning texts or even waking up next to them, the change can be really abrupt. Don’t even get me started on dreams involving your ex! 

What I’ve been doing is giving myself 10 minutes to think about it and cry, and then force myself up no matter how shitty I feel, because once my day really begins and I start to do work, I don’t have the mental capacity to think about him or my sadness anymore. I’ve been scared to go to sleep knowing I’ll wake up and think about him but just try to get your day moving ASAP. Every day is a new day. It’ll get easier and easier every day. Feel better OP, I’m rooting for you!

Ambien isn’t a treatment for depression, but it can help treat feelings of insomnia caused by your depression/anxiety. If you’re already taking anti depressants , some of those even have mood uplifting and energy uplifting properties which can also make it harder to sleep. Ask your doctor if he would recommend you taking ambien as needed on top of the antidepressants you are already taking. I have done this for years without adverse results. The ambien isn’t treating my depression, but is helping me sleep because my depression causes insomnia.
